conviction_note: Peer and company volume data point to a modest Q3 revenue beat (about +3% against a ~$216M bar). But this name sold its last big beat: Q2 was +11% after hours and only +2.4% at the close. The quarter is also not what the stock trades on now. Since 7 Oct it has fallen on the China-ties report, a FINRA fine, class actions and a resale overhang. The swing factor is therefore whether the release's October metrics show account or deposit erosion, and no source gives that number. abs_move 9.5 (implied 8.31, raised for a new period plus the first post-report metrics). p_up 54: a small lean from proxies, held near 50 because call skew already prices upside. Findings sum +0.9 against a scaled +0.76; the two agree.

expectations.real_bar: Two things are needed for the stock to rise. Revenue must come in at or above ~$216M with margin held. And the October / quarter-to-date metrics in the release must show that funded accounts, net deposits and options activity did not erode after the 7 Oct House China report and competitors' transfer incentives. A clean quarter alone was sold last time.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Q4 2026 revenue of about $231M, derived from FY2026 consensus $806.19M (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/bull/forecast/) less Q1 $159.9M, Q2 $198.8M and Q3 consensus ~$216M. This is a derived figure, not quoted.
next_guide.company_current_guide: none. Webull gave no formal revenue or profit guidance on the Q2 call (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262119433-tradingkey). Its only forward statements were: marketing for the rest of 2026 'similar in quantum to the first half', operating leverage to continue, and volumes 'will not revert' to pre-PDT levels.
next_guide.basis: Webull has never issued a numeric guide, so the forward read will be the quarter-to-date commentary and the latest month's metrics table, which the Q2 deck carried through July. It is unclear whether those metrics hold up after the 7 Oct report. HOOD's October showed flat equity and options activity month on month.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue should modestly beat the ~$216M bar. Webull's own July 2026 options volume was 88.7M contracts (flat on June's 89.4M, against a Q2 monthly average of 71M), per the Q2 deck. Robinhood's Q3 options contracts rose 17% QoQ (774M to 905M) from a similar July step-up. Webull's Q1-Q2 trading revenue fits ~$0.68 per options contract, so a ~249M-contract Q3 gives trading revenue of ~$172M (Q2 $147.7M). With interest of ~$42M and other ~$8.5M, total revenue comes to ~$222M, about 3% above $215.6-216.9M. It would be well above FXEmpire's $199M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat by ~20% (198.8 vs ~165.7): +11% after hours, +2.43% at the next close. Q1 2026 revenue +36% with a GAAP loss: -6.51%. Revenue beats have been only partly paid.
findings.why_not_priced: July is public and HOOD reported on 2026-10-27, so analysts should hold most of this. Two things suggest they do not fully: consensus sources still range from $199M to $217M, and the 20-day -21.6% fall was driven by the China report and the FINRA fine, not by volume data. If a beat were fully expected, the bar would sit near $222M rather than $216M.

The House Select Committee report of 2026-10-07 called Webull's China ties a national security risk. Robinhood and SoFi then offered transfer incentives aimed at Webull customers. Webull's 2026-10-09 statement gave no trading or deposit data. October funded accounts and net deposits are therefore the unknown the stock trades on. Webull's October 2025 comparison is strong: net deposits $1.7B, equity $93.2B, options 58.7M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior post-shock metrics release. The report day itself was -19% to $5.89 (https://www.wealthmanagement.com/regulation-compliance/finra-fines-webull-42-million-over-aml-failures context; https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/09/webull-is-still-down-35-this-year-did-today-mark-the-bottom-for-bull-stock/). Scotiabank's upgrade day, 2026-10-09, was +6.05% (baseline).

A stock already 23% down in a month, at its 52-week low, with mean targets 140% above spot, is priced for some attrition. Sized slightly negative and wide, because which way the number lands is not knowable from public data.

findings.finding: Robinhood's October 2026 metrics (published 2026-11-12) show US retail activity holding into Q4. Equity notional was $325.5B against $323.6B in September; options contracts 288.6M against 287.9M; event contracts rose 5% month on month; crypto volume fell 21% month on month. Webull's industry backdrop for Q4-to-date commentary is therefore flat, not falling.
findings.link: Same product and channel: US self-directed retail brokerage paid through PFOF on options and equities. Webull's US accounts are about 85% of 5.03M funded accounts, and the US is about 89% of external revenue. Crypto is ~1% of Webull revenue, so the crypto decline barely transmits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior instance of Webull quarter-to-date commentary moving the stock that I could source. Q2's August 'trending along June' remark did not hold the +11% after-hours move.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since 2026-11-12, so the industry level is priced. What is not priced is whether Webull kept its share of that activity after 7 Oct. That is finding 2, so this one stays small.
findings.independence: Robinhood Q3 release: 'entering Q4 with strong momentum' (https://finviz.com/news/409270/robinhood-reports-third-quarter-2026-results). Shares a peer family with finding 1, but uses a different period and a different document.

findings.finding: The setup into the print is extreme. Spot $4.64 is 0.11% above the 52-week low, -21.6% over 20 days and -54.8% from the high. The mean target is $11.25 (4 Buy, none Sell). Shorts covered from 41.6M to 35.0M into the decline. Calls are bid: skew -16.6 vol points and put/call open interest 0.17. A quarter with no new negative could trigger a relief move, but the call-heavy book is retail and could also unwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the -19% report day, the Scotiabank upgrade produced +6.05% on 2026-10-09. A broker rebound produced +3% on 2026-11-09 (24/7 Wall St). Relief rallies have happened but have not held.
findings.why_not_priced: The fall was driven by regulatory and legal headlines, not by any change in revenue estimates (FY2026 consensus still $806M). A depressed multiple into a likely revenue beat is a real asymmetry. The call skew shows retail already positioned for upside, which is why this stays under 1 point.
findings.independence: Price path and short interest: https://massive.com/quote/bull (2026-11-19). Skew and put/call open interest: sealed baseline.

findings.finding: There is a known resale seller in the window. Country Group Holdings got 12.29M Class A shares (~2.5% of Class A) for Webull's 2026-08-31 purchase of Pi Securities (Thailand). Under the 2026-10-28 amendment it may sell up to 10% of daily volume until 2026-12-24. Webull guarantees $60M of proceeds and pays any shortfall in cash; 12.29M x $4.64 = $57M, so a cash shortfall of at least ~$3M is already locked in. Webull also holds a right to repurchase the block at VWAP.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolable. The stock fell from $6.295 (2026-10-15) to $5.56 (2026-10-27) while the block was registered and selling began.
findings.why_not_priced: The seller is public, so mostly priced. In the window, its ~1M shares a day of potential supply (10% of the 9.6M average volume) caps a relief rally. The lesson-4 question was asked: this was acquisition consideration, not financing distress. Pi Securities buys Thai expansion, and the cash guarantee is small against $701.6M of cash at June 30.
findings.independence: Original prospectus, 2026-10-16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866364/000121390026110295/ea0308679-424b3_webull.htm): $80M of shares at $8.4605, close 2026-08-31. Same filing family, so one finding.

findings.finding: Regulatory and legal overhang from the quarter after Q3 is likely to be addressed on the call. FINRA fined Webull $4.2M on 2026-11-05 over AML, identity theft and best-execution failures for 2020-2023, including no execution-quality review for non-marketable orders (up to 70% of flow). Webull must hire an independent consultant. Securities class actions cover purchases from 2025-04-26 to 2026-10-06, with a lead-plaintiff deadline of 2026-12-07.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The fine day was down about 11% intraday (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/12/3402318/32716/en/bull-investor-alert-webull-hit-with-finra-aml-fine-stock-slides-again-securities-class-action-pending-hbss.html).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced as a headline. The $4.2M is immaterial and falls in Q4, not the reported quarter. What is unpriced is any legal accrual, consultant cost or added compliance spend in Q4 commentary. It is a one-off with no stated path to guidance, so it is sized at a fraction.

findings.finding: Interest-related income likely edged down in Q3. The margin balance fell from $990M in June to $926M in July, and client bank deposits from $3,872M to $3,818M (Q2 deck). Robinhood's Q3 net interest revenue fell 9% YoY on lower short-term rates and securities lending. Q2 interest-related income was $42.8M (21% of revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated in any prior reaction. This line has not been the trading line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small, and the July balances are public, so this is likely mostly in consensus. Filed so the revenue read in finding 1 is net of it; finding 1 already assumes interest of ~$42M.
findings.independence: Robinhood Q3 net interest revenue -9% YoY (https://finviz.com/news/409270/robinhood-reports-third-quarter-2026-results). Shares the Q2 deck with finding 1; this covers a different line.

findings.finding: Prediction markets are a small growing line. Management put prediction-market revenue at $5-6M a quarter in Q2, 'grows significantly month-over-month'. Robinhood's Q3 event-contract revenue rose more than 6x YoY to $173M, and its event contracts rose another 5% month on month in October.
findings.link: Same product: event contracts sold to US retail. Webull offers them through Kalshi. It is ~3% of Webull's Q2 revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small and rarely modelled separately. A doubling from $5-6M adds ~$5M, about 2% of revenue. Overlaps finding 1 only through the 'other revenue' assumption.

findings.finding: There is a buyback lever at the 52-week low. $100M was authorized on 2026-04-21, and only 1,820,788 shares ($11.0M, average $6.03) had been repurchased by 2026-06-30. That leaves ~$89M, about 3.5% of the $2.52B market cap, against $701.6M of cash. Any Q3 repurchase or an acceleration announced with results would offset the CGH supply.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback announcement on 2026-04-21 traded +9% pre-market (https://www.rttnews.com/3640745/webull-authorized-100-mln-share-buyback-stock-gains-in-pre-market.aspx) but closed +0.14% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Unused capacity is public. Whether Webull used it in Q3 or Q4 is not, and an announcement could come with the release. The previous buyback headline's fade argues for keeping this small.
findings.independence: Remaining capacity is also stated in the 2026-10-16 prospectus (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1866364/000121390026110295/ea0308679-424b3_webull.htm). Same issuer documents.

findings.finding: Webull's only statement after the Q2 call (2026-10-09, a 6-K) disputes the committee's process and says 'The report does not change how Webull operates'. It gives no trading, account or deposit data and no reaffirmation of any outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. Filed because it is the only management statement after the last call, and it is silent on metrics, which leaves finding 2 open.

findings.why_not_priced: It is immaterial and a scheduled plan. Filed for completeness, at 0.

baseline_tension: The modest positive lean agrees with the call-side skew (-16.6) and pulls against the -21.6% 20-day run-up. Because the option market already pays for upside, the agreement is a reason to hold p_up near 50 (54), not to raise it.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction) together with lesson 6 (disputed bar: $199M vs $216M): the reported-quarter revenue finding is cut from +1.5 to +1.0. Q2's 20% beat bought only +2.43% at the close.
Lessons 3 and 7 (the lean agrees with an already call-bid skew): p_up is moved from 55 to 54, so expected_move goes from 0.95 to 0.76.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the CGH resale was checked as acquisition consideration for Pi Securities, not distress. Its sign stays a small negative, for supply in the window only.
FPI reaction-history lesson: the base rate was rebuilt from the two confirmed 2026 releases. abs_move is left at 9.5 against the 8.31 straddle.
